Package frc.robot.commands

Class AimPrep

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.commands.AimPrep
public class AimPrep extends Object
Runs turret tracking and shooter spin-up simultaneously until interrupted.

What This Does

Pressing the gunner's left trigger starts two things in parallel:
  1. Turret tracking â€” Turret.track(StateManager) continuously solves for the required turret angle each loop cycle and drives the mechanism toward it. Tracking stays "coarse" (larger position tolerance) until the shooter is also at speed, then tightens.
  2. Shooter spin-up â€” Shooter.shoot(java.util.function.Supplier) asks the aim pipeline for the required hood angle and wheel speed each loop and drives both. The shooter keeps running if interrupted (see Shooter.shoot javadoc) to maintain wheel speed for a follow-up shot.
The command runs indefinitely â€” the scheduler interrupts it when the trigger is released or when a higher-priority command needs the turret or shooter.

Why Parallel, Not Sequence?

Turret slew and shooter spin-up are independent mechanisms that both need to be ready before the shot is fired. Running them in sequence (turret first, then shooter) would waste time â€” the shooter might need 1â€“2 seconds to reach speed, and the turret might need 0.5 seconds to slew. Parallel cuts the worst-case time to max(turret_time, shooter_time).

How to Know When to Fire

This command does NOT feed the ball. After pressing the aim trigger, the gunner presses the left bumper to trigger ShootWhenReady, which waits until RobotStateMachine.isShootReady() is true (both turret tracked and shooter at speed) before starting the hopper.

Subsystem Requirements

Commands.parallel() inherits the requirements of all sub-commands. This command requires both the Turret and Shooter subsystems, preventing other commands from accidentally driving either while aiming.
